name: Muse Number Five — five Muse.ai slot manual scenario
purpose: Proposed manual coverage for five Muse.ai WebView profiles and the separate sixth Group tab. This JSON records no execution result.

release_gate.note: The source describes this 22-step slot flow as a release gate. Detailed D11 acceptance criteria were not supplied. Do not mark passed until the owner supplies criteria and a real run records evidence.

preconditions: Use a non-production test build with internet access.
Do not enter real credentials during initial smoke tests or claim complete security isolation based on separate tabs.
Confirm whether the installed Android System WebView provider supports AndroidX WebKit multi-profile before testing session separation.

steps.action: Install/open the test build.
steps.expected: App launches without asserting release readiness.

steps.action: Inspect primary navigation.
steps.expected: Five Muse tabs and one separate Group tab are presented.

steps.action: Select Muse 1.
steps.expected: Slot 1 opens https://muse.ai/ with profile muse-slot-1.

steps.action: Select Muse 2.
steps.expected: Slot 2 opens https://muse.ai/ with profile muse-slot-2.

steps.action: Select Muse 3.
steps.expected: Slot 3 opens https://muse.ai/ with profile muse-slot-3.

steps.action: Select Muse 4.
steps.expected: Slot 4 opens https://muse.ai/ with profile muse-slot-4.

steps.action: Select Muse 5.
steps.expected: Slot 5 opens https://muse.ai/ with profile muse-slot-5.

steps.action: Confirm Muse page loading and interactive content.
steps.expected: The Muse.ai page loads with JavaScript and DOM storage enabled.

steps.action: Navigate from Muse 1 to Muse 2 and back.
steps.expected: Each tab retains its own WebView instance and selected slot mapping.

steps.action: Simulate or test a network failure on a Muse slot.
steps.expected: A clear connection error appears and tapping it retries https://muse.ai/.

steps.action: Check multi-profile support on the installed WebView provider.
steps.expected: Supported provider opens the Muse page; unsupported provider shows an update message and does not silently use a shared default profile.

steps.action: On supported devices, test slot profile separation with approved test accounts.
steps.expected: Each slot keeps only its own test session and browser storage; do not infer complete security isolation.

steps.action: Inspect Group tab position.
steps.expected: Group is a sixth tab, separate from the five Muse slots.

steps.action: Inspect Group label and semantic glyph.
steps.expected: Label reads Group and glyph communicates group/chat; exact artwork may vary.

steps.action: Inspect Group page index contract.
steps.expected: Group corresponds to zero-based page index 5.

steps.action: Open Group without relay configuration.
steps.expected: A clear not-connected state appears; no send action is available.

steps.action: Revisit each slot after navigation.
steps.expected: Each tab still maps to its matching named profile; record any observed state bleed.

steps.action: Exercise permitted lifecycle transitions in the test build.
steps.expected: No crash or misleading identity after activity recreation or process restart; record session results.

steps.action: Review accessible labels and focus across tabs.
steps.expected: Controls have understandable Muse 1–Muse 5 and Group labels and focus behavior.

steps.action: Try HTTP and external-app URL schemes from a Muse slot.
steps.expected: Non-HTTPS schemes do not open another app; HTTPS navigation remains in the selected WebView.

steps.action: Capture actual build/device/WebView versions, results, logs, and defects.
steps.expected: Evidence is attributable to the exact tested artifact and environment.

steps.action: Ask the source owner to supply D11 criteria and assess all required evidence.
steps.expected: Release gate remains blocked unless approved D11 requirements are met and documented.
